title: Generic extension property under affine ind-étale limits
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $t\in A$, and let $N\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a smooth separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with no quasi-compactness assumption. Separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $N[1/t]=N\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A[1/t]$ [def-pc-base-change]. Suppose restriction is bijective $\operatorname{Hom}_A(X,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A[1/t]}(X[1/t],N[1/t])$ for every smooth $A$-scheme $X$. Let $A\to B$ be ind-étale, meaning a small filtered colimit of finitely presented étale $A$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Then restriction is bijective $\operatorname{Hom}_B(Y,N_B)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{B[1/t]}(Y[1/t],N_B[1/t])$ for every smooth $B$-scheme $Y$. Here $N_B=N\times_A\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $Y[1/t]=Y\times_B\operatorname{Spec}B[1/t]$. Localizing at $t$ means inverting its nonnegative powers; finite presentation means finitely many algebra generators and relations on affine charts. The same assertion holds for the two maps $D\to D\otimes_R D$ and for all maps inserting one factor into $D^{\otimes_R n}$, when $R$ is a local commutative ring and $D$ is a strict henselization of $R$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], with $A$ replaced by $D$, $t$ by any element of $D$, and $B$ by the target ring; these are ind-étale maps by base change and composition.

proof.text: Choose a small filtered presentation $B=\operatorname{colim}_i B_i$ by finitely presented etale $A$-algebras. Reindex it by a nonempty directed set using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal]; this preserves the colimit and all its structural maps. For every $B$-scheme $T$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_B(T,N_B)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(T,N)$, and identifies their restrictions after inverting $t$. We will use these identifications throughout. Since $N/A$ is smooth, it is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; therefore [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion] applies to maps into $N$ from inverse systems of affine $A$-schemes, without any quasi-compactness hypothesis on $N$.

First let $Y=\operatorname{Spec}C$ be smooth over $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $B\to C$ is a smooth ring map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-filtered-colimit-descent] to get $i$ and a smooth $B_i$-algebra $C_i$ with $C\simeq C_i\otimes_{B_i}B$. For $j\geq i$ set $C_j=C_i\otimes_{B_i}B_j$ and $Y_j=\operatorname{Spec}C_j$. The maps $B_j\to C_j$ are smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Each $\operatorname{Spec}B_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale in the sense of [def-weil-etale-morphism] (the notion used by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]), hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; the affine comparison makes $A\to B_j$ smooth. Composition of smooth ring maps and the affine comparison now make every $Y_j$ smooth over $A$. This remains true after any later increase of $j$.

source.place: Tag 0CAQ, lemma-smooth-descends-through-colimit; Tags 00T4 and 00TD; morphisms.tex Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize

proof.text: The universal properties give $C=\operatorname{colim}_{j\geq i} C_j$: a compatible family of $B_i$-algebra maps from $C_j=C_i\otimes_{B_i}B_j$ into a ring $E$ is exactly a map $C_i\to E$ and a compatible family $B_j\to E$ agreeing on $B_i$, hence exactly a map $C_i\otimes_{B_i}B\to E$. Similarly $C[1/t]=\operatorname{colim}_{j\geq i}C_j[1/t]$: maps out of each localization are maps out of $C_j$ making the image of $t$ a unit; compatibility and this one unit condition identify the compatible families with maps out of $C[1/t]$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] gives both $Y=\lim_jY_j$ and $Y[1/t]=\lim_jY_j[1/t]$, with affine stages and transitions. These arguments also apply to any tail of this directed system.

source.place: Tag 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit; tensor-product and localization universal properties

proof.text: Given a map $h:Y[1/t]\to N$ over $A$, the surjective part of [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion], applied to the localized affine system of Step 3, gives $j\geq i$ and $h_j:Y_j[1/t]\to N$ whose pullback is $h$. By the fibre-product universal property, $h_j$ is equally an $A[1/t]$-map to $N[1/t]$. Since $Y_j/A$ is smooth by Step 2, the hypothesis of the item extends $h_j$ uniquely to an $A$-map $g_j:Y_j\to N$. Pull back $g_j$ to $Y$ and use Step 1 to obtain a $B$-map $Y\to N_B$. Its restriction is $h$ under the same identifications. This proves surjectivity for every affine smooth $Y/B$.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, surjectivity of (2); agent application to the extension hypothesis

proof.text: For injectivity on this affine $Y$, let $f,g:Y\to N$ have equal restrictions on $Y[1/t]$. Apply the surjective part of [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion] twice to the unlocalized system and pass to a common stage $j$ to represent them by $f_j,g_j:Y_j\to N$. Their localized restrictions become equal at the limit. The injective part of that same criterion for the localized tail implies equality of their representatives in the filtered colimit of sets, so $f_k|_{Y_k[1/t]}=g_k|_{Y_k[1/t]}$ at some $k\geq j$. Here equality in a directed colimit of sets means eventual equality of two representatives. By Step 2, $Y_k/A$ is smooth. Injectivity in the assumed restriction bijection over $A$ gives $f_k=g_k$. Pullback gives $f=g$ on $Y$. No schematic density of $Y[1/t]$ is asserted or used.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, injectivity and surjectivity of (2); agent application to uniqueness

proof.text: For an arbitrary smooth $B$-scheme $Y$ choose an affine open cover $(U_a)$. Every $U_a/B$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Given a map on $Y[1/t]$, Step 4 extends it on each $U_a$ to $f_a:U_a\to N_B$. Cover each open overlap $U_a\cap U_b$ by affine opens $W$; each $W/B$ is smooth by the same restriction lemma. Step 5 shows $f_a|_W=f_b|_W$ since their localized restrictions are the given map. The equality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives equality on the overlap, and its existence clause glues the $f_a$ to $f:Y\to N_B$. Its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the structure map since the two agree on every $U_a$; its localized restriction is the original map for the same reason. If two extensions existed, Step 5 would identify them on every $U_a$ and the equality clause would identify them on $Y$. This proves the asserted bijection with no quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize, final assertion; schemes.tex Tag 01JA and sheaves.tex Tag 00AN, gluing morphisms

proof.text: For the final assertion, [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] presents $D$ as the colimit of pointed etale $R$-algebras. This category is filtered and essentially small by [lem-sc-pointed-etale-small-filtered], so taking a small skeleton makes $R\to D$ ind-etale in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For either structural map $D\to D\otimes_R D$, the map is the base change of $R\to D$ along the other copy of $R\to D$. More generally, put $T_m=D^{\otimes_R m}$: every map $T_m\to T_{m+1}$ inserting a unit in a specified factor is, after the canonical permutation and associativity identifications, $T_m\to T_m\otimes_R D$, a base change of $R\to D$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] makes all these maps ind-etale, as well as their composites from a specified $D$-factor to $T_n$. Apply the already proved assertion to each such map, with its source as base ring and any supplied element $t$ of that source. In particular, with source $D$, this gives precisely both maps to $D\otimes_R D$ and every specified factor map to $D^{\otimes_R n}$, for any $t\in D$, conditional on the same extension hypothesis for $N/D$.
